description: Known answers for the venv Python with jsonschema (tools/toolchain.lock.md section 1.1, row 'python (venv) + jsonschema'; TV-001). Two cases. Case 'requirement': requirements.schema.json is a byte copy of docs/requirements/schema.json at git blob ca049dfb0a4480f8de889fe112add0a2e893915f (commit 4e3f891), so the check does not depend on the repository schema; invalid-requirement.json seeds four faults. Case 'keywords': keywords.schema.json uses every validation keyword that the nine repository schemas under docs/ use (all draft-07; survey of 2026-09-25, corrected 2026-09-26: minProperties, used by docs/plan/tpm.schema.json margin_policy, was missing and is now seeded as entries/16, review INSP-015 finding-1), and keywords-invalid.json seeds one fault per keyword, each in its own array element so that each yields exactly one error. The validator class is selected from the schema's $schema by jsonschema.validators.validator_for, and the schema itself is checked with check_schema. Expected errors were written by hand from the seeded faults before the first run; each is [absolute_path joined by '/', validator keyword], compared as sorted lists. A propertyNames failure is reported by jsonschema at the object's path with the keyword of the failing subschema (here 'pattern').
